checks.observed: Root-index and current-record readers agree after actual PLAN saves; reads write nothing.
Both readers agree at six actual PLAN interruption boundaries when the complete root association is present.
Completed ADD_SOURCE200+50 returns both sources and250 on both routes. Interrupted source acceptance is not accepted here.
Merged PO preparation is associated with both roots and completed results agree.
Counterexample: root indexing alone inherits existing PLAN-only pending reader. Interrupted PO exposes changed task with no pending flag, while current candidate blocks it.
Counterexample: missing PREPARED associations silently expose unconfirmed price32 instead of confirmed16. The index query cannot detect an excluded record.
Counterexample: omission of an entire latest transport-only operation returns a valid but old chain without an error. Revision continuity alone does not prove association completeness.
Both modeled routes ignore unrelated history at0/1000/100000. Index construction is offline setup, not production discovery.
Same real100-revision fixture: root history grows per revision; current read count remains fixed. Saves still scan history on both routes.
Both individually valid root reads can straddle a merged PO commit and produce a mixed-time page. Per-root validation is not a page-wide snapshot.
Five source interruption comparisons: index filtering preserves old reader semantics and does not supply source-acceptance pending protection by itself.

limitations: All data and index maps are in memory; no Wix latency, scan plan, quota or production snapshot acceptance.
rootIds are derived at snapshot construction from known tasks and PREPARED; this is not a deployed incremental writer or approved historical backfill.
Comparison covers procurement component only; discovery, receipt, loan, stock, finance and whole-page consistency remain separate dependencies.
The root-index route reuses existing confirmedPurchaseState and deliberately adds no new save semantics.
Current-state candidate still has extra updates and unsupported writers; neither route reduces durable history capacity.
decision: Neither production-ready. Test root-associated reader first as the smaller option, but complete dependency/index coverage and PO/source pending semantics before rollout. Current-record design remains offline alternative, not default deployment.
